item.title: FSU vs NC State: Snap counts for the Seminoles
item.description: Saturday's game against the NC State Wolfpack did not go the way the FSU Seminoles were hoping for, with them suffering a 28-10 loss in Doak Campbell Stadium. The loss dropped them to 5-6 overall, and they will finish ACC play 3-5, their third straight losing season in conference play. The Seminoles started the game with a touchdown on offense, but they were unable to sustain the early success, finishing the game with just 283 yards of offense. The running game was nonexistsent, with Zay Parks carrying the ball eight times for 35 yards and the first touchdown of his career. The defense started out strong, but fell apart in the second half, allowing three straight touchdowns as they ran out of gas. NC State quarterback CJ Bailey made them pay for any mistakes they made, completeting 23 of his 36 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns. With 63 plays on offense and 82 on defense, here is a look at the complete snap count for the Seminoles, via Pro Football Focus. Quarterback Ashton Daniels: 63 Running Back Zay Parks: 53 Wide Receiver Micahi Danzy: 61 Jayvan Boggs: 59 Jasen Lopez: 56 Tae'Shaun Gelsey: 7 Devin Carter: 6 Teriq Mallory: 3 Tight End Desirrio Riles: 31 Landen Thomas: 21 Chase Loftin: 18 Offensive Line Xavier Chaplin: 63 André Otto: 63 Nate Pabst: 63 Paul Bowling: 63 Chavez Thompson: 63 Defensive Line Jalen Anderson: 70 Darryll Desir: 66 Daniel Lyons: 60 Deamontae Diggs: 47 Mandrell Desir: 35 Deante McCray: 16 Cam Brooks: 14 Jordan Sanders: 12 Luke Francis Jr.: 12 Jaemin Pinckney: 9 Linebacker Chris Jones: 65 Omar Graham Jr.: 47 Caleb LaVallee: 33 Mikai Gbayor: 20 Defensive Back Nehemiah Chandler: 81 CJ Richard Jr.: 77 Charles Lester III: 77 Ma'Khi Jones: 66 Ashlynd Barker: 66 K.J. item.title: Liga leaders Barca mount impressive Villarreal comeback win
item.description: Villarreal defender Pau Navarro's own goal handed Barcelona the three points in their La Liga win at Camp Nou (Josep LAGO) Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first half penalty. However the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro's own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. "We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I'll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn't happen again," Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. "Against a team like this you can't always turn things around from two down." The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Fermin Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance to send the visitors ahead. Two minutes later Villarreal doubled their advantage when Tani Oluwaseyi, another Canadian, broke in down the left flank and smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net. Hansi Flick's side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. Yamal took it himself but dragged his effort against the post and wide. The winger tried to make amends with a burst inside from the wing before half-time but Peter Gulacsi palmed away his cross-shot and the goalkeeper and his defence combined to thwart Eric Garcia on the follow up. - Quickfire treble - Barcelona came out invigorated in the second half and quickly dragged themselves back into the match. Pedri shot wide and Gulacsi saved from Lopez's low effort before Martin found the net in the 57th minute. Pedri crossed the ball in from the left for the defender to head home. Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro. Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily. Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, ninth, left frustrated. "The (first Barca) goal psychologically killed us, they gained confidence, a couple of minutes later they equalised and from there it's a lot more difficult," C

item.title: Sabah dare to dream as Valdas Dambrauskas plots historic Champions League giant-killing against Barcelona
item.description: Manchester United v Sabah FC - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 - Getty Images Sport Sabah head coach Valdas Dambrauskas is refusing to treat the upcoming visit of Barcelona as a mere exhibition, insisting his side can secure a legendary Champions League result. The Azerbaijani outfit are preparing to host the Catalan giants in front of a capacity crowd in Baku, with the hosts determined to upset the established European order. Dambrauskas refuses to be overawed by Blaugrana The arrival of Hansi Flick’s side in Azerbaijan has dominated the local headlines, but Dambrauskas is focused purely on the competitive aspect of the fixture. While acknowledging the magnitude of the task, the Lithuanian coach is adamant that his players will not step onto the pitch simply to admire their world-class opponents. The former Ludogorets boss believes that the spirit of the Champions League is built on precisely these kinds of David versus Goliath encounters. The manager admitted that the pressure of the job often weighs heavily on him, though this specific continental stage offers a different kind of motivation. "Sometimes I can't sleep because of anxiety, especially before the Azerbaijan league games, but matches like this in the Champions League we simply have to enjoy," Dambrauskas explained, as quoted by Sport . However, he was quick to clarify that enjoyment does not equate to a lack of competitive fire, adding: "Our goal is to win every game, regardless of the opponent or the expected result." A rallying cry to the Baku faithful Understanding the significance of home advantage, Dambrauskas has issued a direct appeal to the Sabah fanbase to create a hostile environment for Hansi Flick's side. The coach wants the stands to be packed to the rafters, providing the energy needed to sustain his players through what is expected to be a grueling ninety minutes of football against one of the most technical teams in the world. "It is a big game for the fans, for us, for the players and for the coaching staff. We are going to enjoy it together, believe and give everything we have," the manager stated. He is leaning into the romanticism of the underdog story, suggesting that the sport's inherent lack of predictability is exactly why his team should feel confident. "Sometimes football writes incredible stories, so we are going to go out there and write one on Wednesday," he proclaimed. Timo refuses to hide underdog ambitions The sense of belief within the dressing room is not restricted to the coaching staff, as Sabah player Tymoteusz 'Timo' Puchacz echoed his manager's defiant sentiments. While acknowledging the massive gulf in stature between the two clubs, the midfielder insisted that once the whistle blows, reputations count for very little. He sees the match as a chance to turn a childhood dream into a professional reality by competing as equals. The player confessed that the reality of facing Barcelona still feels somewhat surreal, yet he is focused
item.content:encoded: Manchester United v Sabah FC - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 - Getty Images Sport Sabah head coach Valdas Dambrauskas is refusing to treat the upcoming visit of Barcelona as a mere exhibition, insisting his side can secure a legendary Champions League result. The Azerbaijani outfit are preparing to host the Catalan giants in front of a capacity crowd in Baku, with the hosts determined to upset the established European order. Dambrauskas refuses to be overawed by Blaugrana The arrival of Hansi Flick’s side in Azerbaijan has dominated the local headlines, but Dambrauskas is focused purely on the competitive aspect of the fixture. While acknowledging the magnitude of the task, the Lithuanian coach is adamant that his players will not step onto the pitch simply to admire their world-class opponents. The former Ludogorets boss believes that the spirit of the Champions League is built on precisely these kinds of David versus Goliath encounters. The manager admitted that the pressure of the job often weighs heavily on him, though this specific continental stage offers a different kind of motivation. "Sometimes I can't sleep because of anxiety, especially before the Azerbaijan league games, but matches like this in the Champions League we simply have to enjoy," Dambrauskas explained, as quoted by Sport . However, he was quick to clarify that enjoyment does not equate to a lack of competitive fire, adding: "Our goal is to win every game, regardless of the opponent or the expected result." A rallying cry to the Baku faithful Understanding the significance of home advantage, Dambrauskas has issued a direct appeal to the Sabah fanbase to create a hostile environment for Hansi Flick's side. The coach wants the stands to be packed to the rafters, providing the energy needed to sustain his players through what is expected to be a grueling ninety minutes of football against one of the most technical teams in the world. "It is a big game for the fans, for us, for the players and for the coaching staff. We are going to enjoy it together, believe and give everything we have," the manager stated. He is leaning into the romanticism of the underdog story, suggesting that the sport's inherent lack of predictability is exactly why his team should feel confident. "Sometimes football writes incredible stories, so we are going to go out there and write one on Wednesday," he proclaimed. Timo refuses to hide underdog ambitions The sense of belief within the dressing room is not restricted to the coaching staff, as Sabah player Tymoteusz 'Timo' Puchacz echoed his manager's defiant sentiments. While acknowledging the massive gulf in stature between the two clubs, the midfielder insisted that once the whistle blows, reputations count for very little. He sees the match as a chance to turn a childhood dream into a professional reality by competing as equals. The player confessed that the reality of facing Barcelona still feels somewhat surreal, yet he is focused on maintaining his composure. "It’s hard to even think about it. When I talk to my friends and family, it still seems unreal that we’re going to play against Barcelona . It’s like a dream. Honestly, I’m really looking forward to the match. Because, at the end of the day, it’s just a normal football match. I know, maybe it sounds crazy, but I want to beat Barcelona, ​​but why not?" Timo stated. Chasing a miracle in Azerbaijan The tactical battle will be immense, as Sabah must find a way to neutralise one of the most potent attacking forces in world football. Dambrauskas will likely look to a compact defensive shape to frustrate the visitors, hoping to exploit any complacency that might creep into the Barcelona ranks. Every minute that the score remains level will only increase the belief within the stadium that an upset is truly possible. Ultimately, the match represents more than just three points for the hosts; it is a chance to prove that the gap in European football is closing. If Sabah can maintain their focus and execute their game plan, they might just deliver the "incredible story" their manager has promised.

item.title: Protesters storm Meta offices in India
item.description: Members of the opposition Congress party protested outside Meta's offices in Delhi on Friday and appear to have entered the building in a video shared by CNN . Members of the party's youth wing are demanding the company restore accounts of party leaders and warned of more protests to come. The Congress party has criticized Meta for censoring speech that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his BJP party disagree with, and has placed banners accusing Mark Zuckerberg of favoring BJP around the city. While two accounts in question were restored Friday, Manu Jain, who oversees social media for the party's youth wing, told Reuters that "thousands of … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Minnesota vs. Northwestern: The Elite, The Meh & The Ugly
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Golden Gophers running back TJ Thomas (23) runs the ball as Northwestern Wildcats defensive back Braden Turner (9) defends during the second half at Huntington Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Golden Gophers (6-5) played their final home game of the season and sent the seniors out on a winning note with a 20-17 victory over the Northwestern Wildcats (6-5). The Elite Luke Drzewiecki. Through the first seven games of the season, Drzewiecki was automatic. He was a perfect 15-of-15 on field goal attempts, including a 60-yarder in the final seconds of regulation on the road against Indiana. Then came a pair of 56-yard misses against UCLA, before finishing that game 2-of-4 on field goal attempts. Drzewiecki looked broken in the first half of the Northwestern game, pushing a 48-yard attempt wide left before missing a 53-yard attempt that fell well short of the uprights. But when it mattered most, he delivered, nailing the 44-yard game-winner as time expired. Walk off W‼️ Luke Drzewiecki drills it from 44 yards for the win 🙌 pic.twitter.com/XPMyNCQ8wg — Minnesota on BTN (@MinnesotaOnBTN) November 21, 2026 Darius Taylor. It’s been a disappointing season for the fourth-year running back, but he showed flashes of his old self a week ago against Penn State. Saturday’s Senior Day performance was vintage Darius Taylor, as he was patient behind his offensive line, elusive between the tackles, and used his legs to fight through tackles and pick up extra yards. He rushed for a season-high 108 yards on 15 carries. T.J. Thomas. The former Elon transfer has been the Gophers’ best running back in space this season, and Minnesota frequently called his number on toss plays against the Wildcats. It put the ball in his hands in space and allowed him to find the open running lane and accelerate through it. With Taylor working between the tackles, Thomas gave the offense a change-of-pace back who could attack the perimeter, and he finished the game with 61 rushing yards on 10 carries. Jerome Williams. It’s no secret that Bennett Warren has been overmatched at left guard, where he is playing out of position. He was replaced before halftime a week ago in State College, with fourth-year lineman Jerome Williams taking over. I don’t think it’s a coincidence that the offense found its footing coming out of the locker room for the second half, yet Warren got the start again on Saturday against Northwestern. Williams replaced him again midway through the second quarter and suddenly quarterback Drake Lindsey had time to get comfortable in the pocket, going 5-of-6 for 42 passing yards on that drive. Warren isn’t to blame for all of the issues on the offensive line, but clearly Williams raises the floor for the line and has played well enough to make his first career start in next week’s regular season finale. item.content:encoded: Nov 21, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Golden Gophers running back TJ Thomas (23) runs the ball as Northwestern Wildcats defensive back Braden Turner (9) defends during the second half at Huntington Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Golden Gophers (6-5) played their final home game of the season and sent the seniors out on a winning note with a 20-17 victory over the Northwestern Wildcats (6-5). The Elite Luke Drzewiecki. Through the first seven games of the season, Drzewiecki was automatic. But when it mattered most, he delivered, nailing the 44-yard game-winner as time expired. Walk off W‼️ Luke Drzewiecki drills it from 44 yards for the win 🙌 pic.twitter.com/XPMyNCQ8wg — Minnesota on BTN (@MinnesotaOnBTN) November 21, 2026 Darius Taylor. It’s been a disappointing season for the fourth-year running back, but he showed flashes of his old self a week ago against Penn State. Saturday’s Senior Day performance was vintage Darius Taylor, as he was patient behind his offensive line, elusive between the tackles, and used his legs to fight through tackles and pick up extra yards. He rushed for a season-high 108 yards on 15 carries. T.J. Thomas. The former Elon transfer has been the Gophers’ best running back in space this season, and Minnesota frequently called his number on toss plays against the Wildcats. It put the ball in his hands in space and allowed him to find the open running lane and accelerate through it. With Taylor working between the tackles, Thomas gave the offense a change-of-pace back who could attack the perimeter, and he finished the game with 61 rushing yards on 10 carries. Jerome Williams. It’s no secret that Bennett Warren has been overmatched at left guard, where he is playing out of position. He was replaced before halftime a week ago in State College, with fourth-year lineman Jerome Williams taking over. I don’t think it’s a coincidence that the offense found its footing coming out of the locker room for the second half, yet Warren got the start again on Saturday against Northwestern. Williams replaced him again midway through the second quarter and suddenly quarterback Drake Lindsey had time to get comfortable in the pocket, going 5-of-6 for 42 passing yards on that drive. Warren isn’t to blame for all of the issues on the offensive line, but clearly Williams raises the floor for the line and has played well enough to make his first career start in next week’s regular season finale. Anthony Smith. The Gophers’ All-Big Ten defensive end made the most of his final game at Huntington Bank Stadium, racking up 2.5 tackles for loss and even recovering his own forced fumble on a strip sack. FUMBLE ‼️ Anthony Smith recovers for @GopherFootball ! Watch on FS1 pic.twitter.com/nKWfKzTLpn — Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) November 21, 2026 Danny Collins. If you read my opponent preview earlier this week, you’ll know I was not optimistic about the Gophers’ chances in a chess match between Northwestern offensive coordinator Chip Kelly and Minnesota defensive coordinator Danny Collins. It wasn’t a perfect performance, as the Gopher defense allowed touchdown drives in the final minutes of both halves. But Collins did not get outcoached as he has been in previous losses this season, leading a defense that forced five punts and one turnover. A win on Senior Day. Always good to send off the seniors with one last win at home. The Gophers are bowl-eligible for the sixth straight season. It’s a small consolation in what has been a disappointing season from a big-picture perspective, but I’d rather go bowling than not, though I assume they’ll only feel more insignificant moving forward in the era of the 24-team playoff. The Meh The post-Greg Harbaugh offense. Tight ends coach Eric Koehler took over offensive play-calling in the wake of Harbaugh’s firing, and his first game at the reins was a mixed bag. The first offensive play of the game — a bubble screen to Roman Voss that lost a yard — didn’t inspire much confidence. And for the second straight week, the Gophers were held scoreless in the first half. But the offense looked much improved in the second half, with the ground game rolling and Lindsey comfortable in the pocket. I especially liked the mix of rushing schemes and the play-calling in the red zone. That said, this team still has not scored more than 20 points since September 26. Jalen Smith reels it in for the @GopherFootball lead 🙌 Watch on FS1 pic.twitter.com/dQ5Azo2X4J — Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) November 21, 2026 Drake Lindsey. It was not a bad performance on paper. The second-year signal caller finished 23-of-37 for 224 passing yards and two touchdowns, and he looked much better in the second half than he did in the first. But Lindsey’s biggest issue remains his inability to see the field. The broadcast team called attention to multiple plays in which Lindsey had a wide open receiver downfield but never saw him. Lindsey also tried to force a couple throws into coverage, but as someone who has been pleading for him to be more aggressive and not so gun shy, I’m not going come down too hard on him for taking risks. Drake Lindsey on his 34-yard late game pass to Noah Jennings to set up the Gophers game winning Field Goal. #RTB #SkiUMah #Gophers pic.twitter.com/6dxZsF1xW6 — Minnesota Football (@GopherFootball) November 21, 2026 The Ugly Javon Tracy’s ill-advised trickeration on a kickoff return. On a kickoff return in the third quarter, Northwestern opted to kick it short, and Tracy decided to throw the ball across the field to Quayd Hendryx. But Hendryx dropped the ball and a Wildcat jumped on it. Fortunately, it was ruled an illegal forward pass and Minnesota was able to keep possession of the ball while simply being assessed a 5-yard penalty. Head coach P.J. Fleck said they had practiced the play during the week, but I think perhaps they should have practiced it some more before giving it the green light in a game.

item.title: Ryan Day and Ross Bjork are lighting money on fire
item.description: LINCOLN, NEBRASKA - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes stands with the team before the game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Lincoln, Nebraska. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is no way to describe Ohio State’s 2026 season as anything other than a spectacular failure. The Buckeyes entered the new campaign with one of the most expensive rosters and coaching staffs in the sport as the clear favorite in the Big Ten, one of the favorites to win the national title and the preseason No. 1 team in the country. Instead, Ohio State is sitting here at 7-4 after being the first ranked program in 32 tries to lose a game to Nebraska. Nobody has saved more head coaching jobs in college football this season than Ryan Day, who has now found ways to lose to Steve Sarkisian, Lincoln Riley, Dan Lanning and Matt Rhule — all in one calendar year! That, however, is a story for another day… The topic at hand is the failed regime that has allowed Ohio State to reach this point. It starts with roster building. I wrote last week that Mark Pantoni deserves some of the blame for the Buckeyes’ disastrous 2026 season, which has now only gotten worse this weekend. That remains true, as he and Day are responsible for deciding which players they want to bring into the program, both via recruiting and the transfer portal. When it comes to the latter, these last two transfer portal classes have been a complete calamity. Ohio State has added 28 players to its roster via the transfer portal these last two offseasons, and virtually none of them have made a positive impact on the field. The Buckeyes have spent millions of dollars on guys like Beau Atkinson, Ethan Onianwa, Cam Calhoun and Phillip Daniels — just to name a few glaring failures of talent identification — and all they have done is make the roster actively worse. This comes on the heels of an almost perfect 2024 transfer portal class, which included superstars like Caleb Downs, Quinshon Judkins and others. That was also, conveniently, the last transfer portal class before Ross Bjork took over as Athletic Director, which I’m sure is just a coincidence… Since Bjork’s arrival, Ohio State has refused to go out and actually land that same level of actual NFL talent, whether via the transfer portal or traditional high school recruiting. We have watched big name after big name spurn the Buckeyes in favor of other programs, simply because the powers that be in Columbus were unwilling to spend a few extra dollars. They brought in Bjork, a failed athletic director at Texas A&M, for his ability to fundraise, but instead he has cut corners. So you get players like Atkinson instead, who having reportedly been giving an NIL deal north of $1 million, has more personal fouls than impact plays in his two years with the program. Even the talented players they do manage to land are wildly mishandled, which brings us to the next point: coaching.
item.content:encoded: LINCOLN, NEBRASKA - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes stands with the team before the game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Lincoln, Nebraska. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is no way to describe Ohio State’s 2026 season as anything other than a spectacular failure. The Buckeyes entered the new campaign with one of the most expensive rosters and coaching staffs in the sport as the clear favorite in the Big Ten, one of the favorites to win the national title and the preseason No. 1 team in the country. Instead, Ohio State is sitting here at 7-4 after being the first ranked program in 32 tries to lose a game to Nebraska. Nobody has saved more head coaching jobs in college football this season than Ryan Day, who has now found ways to lose to Steve Sarkisian, Lincoln Riley, Dan Lanning and Matt Rhule — all in one calendar year! That, however, is a story for another day… The topic at hand is the failed regime that has allowed Ohio State to reach this point. It starts with roster building. I wrote last week that Mark Pantoni deserves some of the blame for the Buckeyes’ disastrous 2026 season, which has now only gotten worse this weekend. That remains true, as he and Day are responsible for deciding which players they want to bring into the program, both via recruiting and the transfer portal. When it comes to the latter, these last two transfer portal classes have been a complete calamity. Ohio State has added 28 players to its roster via the transfer portal these last two offseasons, and virtually none of them have made a positive impact on the field. The Buckeyes have spent millions of dollars on guys like Beau Atkinson, Ethan Onianwa, Cam Calhoun and Phillip Daniels — just to name a few glaring failures of talent identification — and all they have done is make the roster actively worse. This comes on the heels of an almost perfect 2024 transfer portal class, which included superstars like Caleb Downs, Quinshon Judkins and others. That was also, conveniently, the last transfer portal class before Ross Bjork took over as Athletic Director, which I’m sure is just a coincidence… Since Bjork’s arrival, Ohio State has refused to go out and actually land that same level of actual NFL talent, whether via the transfer portal or traditional high school recruiting. We have watched big name after big name spurn the Buckeyes in favor of other programs, simply because the powers that be in Columbus were unwilling to spend a few extra dollars. They brought in Bjork, a failed athletic director at Texas A&M, for his ability to fundraise, but instead he has cut corners. So you get players like Atkinson instead, who having reportedly been giving an NIL deal north of $1 million, has more personal fouls than impact plays in his two years with the program. Even the talented players they do manage to land are wildly mishandled, which brings us to the next point: coaching. This Ohio State roster is undeniably less talented than probably every other team that Ryan Day has had in his time at the helm. That is not an excuse for Day, as he is partially in charge of building said roster, but it is objectively true. However, on top of a much lower ceiling, the Buckeyes have made things even tougher by refusing to play younger guys who are clearly better than the veterans ahead of them. We have seen flash plays in very limited reps from a pair of freshmen in Legend Bey and Khary Wilder — two players at positions Ohio State has struggled at this season. They have shown an explosiveness at running back and defensive line, respectively, that really nobody else on the current roster has given them at any point this year. Their reward? Riding the bench. Neither of them can get on the field with any regularity. The coaching staff will claim they haven’t seen enough in practice to be able to ‘trust’ these guys on game day, but yet I have to watch Isaiah West fumble every week and incompetent defensive line play across the board with seemingly zero repercussions. That same accountability that young guys like Bey and Wilder are held to is not applied to the veterans. West can give the ball away three times in four weeks and still play over Bey. The defensive line can go four weeks without a sack and Wilder still can’t get any snaps. Payton Pierce can play some of the worst football you’ve ever seen and still play critical downs over a much better player in Riley Pettijohn. The list goes on and on. What is the point of recruiting electric, talented players if you aren’t going to play them? It is one of the many failures of this abysmal coaching staff, and with Ohio State’s season now effectively over —with still a chance they lose at home to a very bad Michigan team next weekend — massive changes need to be made. It should start with firing Bjork and Day, but neither of those are likely to happen. In Day’s case, there has never been an easier time for Ohio State to move on. With Jeremiah Smith off to the NFL, there are really only a handful of players set to be on the roster for 2027 that you’d really care all that much about losing. After transition to more of a ‘CEO’ role, Day was supposed to lead the charge on roster construction, coaching staff overview and in-game decision making. All three of those areas are now significantly worse than they were just a few years ago. Day’s own standard he set as Ohio State’s head coach is to complete three key objectives each season: beat Michigan, win the Big Ten, and win the national title. If he isn’t able to pull of a miraculous victory in The Game, he will be 5-for-23 in actually achieving said goals. Holding him to his own words, Day’s tenure has been a failure. Now in his eighth year with the program, Day is 2-4 against Michigan, has not won the Big Ten since the fake 2020 season, and got gifted a national title with a generationally talented roster that basically bullied the coaching staff into a better game plan — which they have since abandoned. Unfortunately, while it is abundantly clear that Ohio State should fire Ryan Day, they are ultimately not going to do it. Bjork is too inept to make an actual tough decision, and so the only thing we can hope for heading into 2027 is wide scale coaching staff changes. And when I said wide scale, I mean each and every member of this current coaching staff needs to be let go. There are zero redeeming qualities among this group, and if Day is going to continue to get dragged down by his own shortcomings, he needs to get some actual adults in the room. On offense, every single one of offensive coordinator Arthur Smith down to every assistant — offensive line coach Tyler Bowen, tight ends coach Keenan Bailey, quarterbacks coach Billy Fessler, running backs coach Carlos Locklyn, and wide receivers coach Cortez Hankton — should all be replaced. Bailey, Bowen and Fessler are the biggest offenders, and I’ve already written ad nauseam about how none of them should have ever been hired at a place like Ohio State in the first place, but they are the clearest examples of guys who under no circumstances can be allowed back in the Woody ever again once this season comes to a merciful close. Locklyn got lucky to have a pair of NFL players in his room in year one in Columbus, but the running back position has since fallen off a cliff, and all the guys in that unit have gotten worse under his tutelage. The same goes for Hankton, who despite recruiting some players with high pedigree, the wide receiver room is in a terrible place after Jeremiah Smith leaves. The same can be said on defense, where Matt Patricia has stolen $3.75 million from the university after Bjork and his cronies rushed to bid against themselves for a guy we can now see was simply gifted one of the most talented Ohio State defenses ever. item.title: NFL fines: 2 Texans, 1 Browns punished for Week 10 actions, includes ‘violent gesture’
item.description: The Cleveland Browns get to enjoy their bye week with no chance of being knocked out of their current NFL playoff position . Sunday’s slate of games is far from exciting for general NFL fans, with a few games that Browns fans will pay attention to because of playoff scenarios. There isn’t even “Rams Watch” for 2027 NFL draft reasons , as the Los Angeles Rams join Cleveland and four other teams on a bye this week. Looking back at the Browns big Week 10 victory , which set the NFL to flex Week 12’s matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders to Sunday Night Football , three players have a little less money in their pockets. The league’s weekly tradition of handing down fines almost a week later continued for Week 10, with two Texans and one Browns player fined for their actions: DT Sam Kamara – Unnecessary Roughness – Use of Helmet – $6,750 WR Nico Collins – Unsportsmanlike Conduct – Violent Gesture – $14,926 DB MJ Stewart – Unnecessary Roughness – Facemask – $11,667 The “violent gesture” Collins was fined for was this celebration, which was also penalized in the game: The NFL fined Texans WR Nico Collins $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct (violent gesture) while celebrating Dalton Schultz’s touchdown last week in Cleveland. Collins was also flagged. pic.twitter.com/TEn8qM8NvK — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 21, 2026 For the season so far, the NFL has levied 263 fines, on just over one percent of plays run this season.

item.title: Confirmed Man United XI vs Liverpool: Maguire, Amad drop to the bench
item.description: Confirmed Man United XI vs Liverpool: Maguire, Amad drop to the bench Manchester United visit Liverpool this afternoon for Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge after joining the club on Wednesday. Here is the confirmed line-up for the game. Goalkeeper and Defence Senne Lammens is in goal. Diogo Dalot is the right-back; Matthijs de Ligt/a> and Pochettino’s compatriot Lisandro Martinez are the centre-backs. Patrick Dorgu is at left-back. Harry Maguire is on the bench. Midfield Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo form the central midfield pivot. Carlos Baleba is out for a few weeks with a hamstring injury and Manuel Ugarte is also a long-term absentee. Attack Bryan Mbeumo, Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Joshua Zirkzee are the front four. Mbeumo will be on the right, with Fernandes in the 10, Cunha on the left and Zirkzee up front. Amad drops to the bench. Benjamin Sesko is out of action until the new year. Marcus Rashford is close to fitness but not yet ready. Substitutes To follow. Final Thoughts To follow. Featured image by Angel Martinez via Getty Images online polls

item.title: What Wake Forest Said After the Georgia Tech Win
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Wake Forest continues to reach lofty levels in the college football world. With the Demon Deacons beating Georgia Tech 50-29 in Atlanta on Saturday afternoon, Wake is now 10-1 overall and 7-1 in ACC play. The Deacs have assured themselves a spot in the ACC championship game in two weeks in Charlotte. But first they have the regular season finale against Duke this Saturday with ESPN College GameDay in the house for only the second time ever (and first with a live crowd). So let’s see what Wake Forest said after the Georgia Tech win. What Wake Forest Said Jake Dickert The head coach said after the game that the locker room celebration was more muted than usual. Wake gave up 249 yards of offense to the Yellowjackets in the second half and was outscored 22-14. “When you look at the totality of the win, I thought it was a good win,” Dickert said after the game. “It’s the first time we have lost a half of football in a long time,” he added, referring back to the first half against Miami on September 18 th . He said the mood after the game has as much to do with the standards of the program now and what the players’ expectations are for themselves. Still, he said, a win is a win. “Don’t undersell winning on the road.” He pointed out that Wake has won six games on the road against Power 4 programs, something Wake claims is a record in the CFP era. The best we could find during that timeframe was other teams that had won five. Dickert said he was proud of only the third team in program history with 10 wins. “The fact that it was a little muted in there, I understand. There’s a lot to play for. We’re excited about what next week brings. But there’s a lot of good things on that field today.” Among the good things was 607 yards of offense against a physical Georgia Tech team. Quarterback Gio Lopez was 17 of 22 passing for 324 yards and two touchdowns. He also had two rushing touchdowns. And that was with sitting the fourth quarter of another blowout. “This guy has not played a four-quarter game in seven weeks.” Dickert pointed out that Lopez did not play against Merrimack with an injured knee, or as Dickert called, “…a stat-stuffing FCS game.” Dickert continued to call Lopez one of the top three players in the country. “I think he’s showing that each and every week.” As he has done throughout much of the season, Dickert deferred any credit for the win, instead giving it to the staff and the players. “I can’t give them that,” Dickert said of the mentality that has been instilled in the players this season. “As coaches, we create the plan. But our guys are the plan. item.content:encoded: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Wake Forest continues to reach lofty levels in the college football world. With the Demon Deacons beating Georgia Tech 50-29 in Atlanta on Saturday afternoon, Wake is now 10-1 overall and 7-1 in ACC play. The Deacs have assured themselves a spot in the ACC championship game in two weeks in Charlotte. But first they have the regular season finale against Duke this Saturday with ESPN College GameDay in the house for only the second time ever (and first with a live crowd). So let’s see what Wake Forest said after the Georgia Tech win. What Wake Forest Said Jake Dickert The head coach said after the game that the locker room celebration was more muted than usual. Wake gave up 249 yards of offense to the Yellowjackets in the second half and was outscored 22-14. “When you look at the totality of the win, I thought it was a good win,” Dickert said after the game. “It’s the first time we have lost a half of football in a long time,” he added, referring back to the first half against Miami on September 18 th . He said the mood after the game has as much to do with the standards of the program now and what the players’ expectations are for themselves. Still, he said, a win is a win. “Don’t undersell winning on the road.” He pointed out that Wake has won six games on the road against Power 4 programs, something Wake claims is a record in the CFP era. The best we could find during that timeframe was other teams that had won five. Dickert said he was proud of only the third team in program history with 10 wins. “The fact that it was a little muted in there, I understand. There’s a lot to play for. We’re excited about what next week brings. But there’s a lot of good things on that field today.” Among the good things was 607 yards of offense against a physical Georgia Tech team. Quarterback Gio Lopez was 17 of 22 passing for 324 yards and two touchdowns. He also had two rushing touchdowns. And that was with sitting the fourth quarter of another blowout. “This guy has not played a four-quarter game in seven weeks.” Dickert pointed out that Lopez did not play against Merrimack with an injured knee, or as Dickert called, “…a stat-stuffing FCS game.” Dickert continued to call Lopez one of the top three players in the country. “I think he’s showing that each and every week.” As he has done throughout much of the season, Dickert deferred any credit for the win, instead giving it to the staff and the players. “I can’t give them that,” Dickert said of the mentality that has been instilled in the players this season. “As coaches, we create the plan. But our guys are the plan. And they’re out there executing and putting in the work each and every week.” Photo courtesy: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Langston Hardy Saturday’s game, particularly the 12 penalties, left a lot for the team to clean up. The starting defensive end looked at what is ahead this week. “I think we realize, even with today, there’s always things we need to improve on.” He said there was time to celebrate the win and then get back to work on Sunday. “We just know that we have to keep our foot on the gas.” He said the 4 th quarter, with the defense giving up 144 yards, was the primary reason the locker room celebration was a little more subdued than usual. “Obviously the fourth quarter is a big emphasis for us, so losing the fourth quarter, we don’t want to see that happen, so that was like the last taste in our mouth from the game.” Hardy said linebacker Aiden Hall led the thought process about moving past the heartbreaking loss to Georgia Tech last year when a penalty was not called in a critical moment of the game. “He was talking about we’re not going to let them dictate the game this year. We were going to go out there and have a fast start, fly around and be physical.” Gio Lopez The quarterback had a big statistical day. But he deferred to what the offense is doing as a whole. “I think it’s just executing at a high level,” he said. He acknowledged there are elements that require film study and cleanup. “Overall, we’re executing at a high level and understanding what’s asked of us on each play.” “I didn’t know that. That’s pretty cool,” Lopez said when asked about this being only the third time in program history that Wake Forest has hit double digits in wins. It’s also the most wins he has ever had in his college career. There is a lot more potential ahead, obviously. “It’s been really fun. This opportunity that Coach Dickert and Coach Ezell gave me. I’m forever grateful for that. It’s the team I’m on, the group of guys that just love playing for one another.” He talked about the potential to go 11-1, with a win over Duke, and what it would represent. “The brotherhood we have is the best part of this team.” Main Image: Brett Davis-Imagn Images

item.title: Hull's Tzolakis having the game of his life to keep Brighton at bay 🧤
item.description: Hull's Tzolakis having the game of his life to keep Brighton at bay 🧤 In any normal game, Brighton would be leading at the break against Hull City. However, Konstantinos Tzolakis is having the game of his life as he single handledly keeps the Tigers in the contest. The high-flying Seagulls have broken an unwanted first-half record for the season but have yet to break the deadlock. The Greek shot stopper has made a series of stunning saves, keeping out close to two expected goals combined. Brighton have a Greek star of their own though in Charalampos Kostoulas, who could yet come on and usurp his international teammate as the match winner. Can Hull's outfield players match their keeper, or will it remain a one-man show at the back?

item.title: UCLA Coach Makes Eye-Opening Bryce Underwood Admission After Michigan Upset
item.description: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood has taken plenty of criticism this season, but following Saturday’s stunning 18-16 triple-overtime victory over No. 4 UCLA, he received some major praise from an unexpected source. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney didn’t hesitate when asked about Michigan’s performance following the Bruins’ first loss of the season. In fact, Chesney had some particularly encouraging words about the Wolverines’ sophomore quarterback. “I thought Bryce [Underwood] had an unbelievable day today,” Chesney said during his postgame press conference . “I thought he threw some balls in some tight windows, including that last play.” That’s a pretty strong endorsement from a coach whose defense had been among the nation’s toughest to score against. Nov 21, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; UCLA head coach Bob Chesney talks with Line Judge Sergio DeHoyos during the first quarter against Michigan at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bryce Underwood Earns Respect After Difficult Stretch Underwood’s performance wasn’t exactly eye-popping statistically, as he completed 11 of 24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown. However, he delivered when Michigan needed him most, connecting with Jalen Hoffman on the game-winning two-point conversion in the third overtime. The performance was especially meaningful considering Underwood’s recent struggles and the quarterback controversy surrounding Michigan’s offense. After losing his starting job earlier this season , Underwood returned to the starting lineup against the previously undefeated Bruins and helped deliver Michigan’s biggest victory of the year. According to the official UCLA game recap , the Bruins entered Saturday with a perfect 10-0 record. Underwood’s decisive completion ended that unbeaten run and improved Michigan to 6-5, making the Wolverines bowl eligible. Chesney also credited Michigan’s physical defense and the toughness of the Wolverines’ overall performance. Still, his praise for Underwood stood out because UCLA had held Michigan to just 247 total yards and fewer than 50 percent completions. With Michigan preparing for its rivalry showdown against Ohio State , Underwood still has plenty to prove. But after everything he has experienced this season, hearing that kind of praise from the opposing head coach has to feel pretty good. And for Michigan fans hoping Underwood can become the quarterback they envisioned, Saturday was a much-needed step in the right direction.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama Throws Shade At NBA Stars After 50-Point Game: “I’m Not Very Good At Stat Padding”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama delivered a playful jab at his NBA peers after scoring 50 points in the San Antonio Spurs ’ 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday, suggesting his approach to individual statistics has limited his milestone performances . The Spurs superstar finished with 19 rebounds, five blocks, four steals, and one assist alongside his scoring outburst. He shot 20-of-29 from the field and 5-of-11 from three-point range, producing a dominant performance in just 32 minutes. “It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding. So I haven’t reached it as many times as I should have.” Wembanyama did not identify anyone as the target of that remark. However, the comment added another layer to a remarkable night that helped San Antonio improve to 14-3, matching the NBA’s best record. This was his second 50-point performance of the season and the third of his career. He previously scored a career-high 52 against the Dallas Mavericks on November 4. His latest effort tied David Robinson for the second-most 50-point games in Spurs history, behind George Gervin’s five. Wembanyama established control early, scoring 17 first-quarter points before reaching halftime with 32 points and 13 rebounds. The Spurs led 61-45 at the break, with their centerpiece influencing the game at both ends. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. “That step-back three that I took, it doesn’t correlate with this. It didn’t fit the definition, for example. So I did try, at the end, yeah, I did try to get a three when I had 47 points.” That admission gave his earlier remark an amusing contradiction. Wembanyama had teased others about chasing numbers, then openly conceded that he wanted the extra three points himself. He defended that instinct by referencing Wilt Chamberlain . “I don’t think Wilt thought about that when he had 98 points. I don’t think he thought about making the extra pass.” There is a reasonable distinction between enjoying a milestone and compromising a team’s chances to reach one. Wembanyama’s scoring came with exceptional efficiency, overwhelming rebounding, and substantial defensive production in a comfortable victory. His contribution extended far beyond the points column. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson also acknowledged that removing him just short of 50 would have been difficult, while emphasizing the importance of avoiding unnecessary injury risk. Ultimately, Wembanyama gave fans both a spectacular performance and a memorable sound bite. The stat-padding remark invited debate, but his willingness to admit chasing the final basket kept it from becoming a simple lecture directed at everyone else. At 22, he is already producing nights that require very little embellishment.

The Spurs superstar finished with 19 rebounds, five blocks, four steals, and one assist alongside his scoring outburst. He shot 20-of-29 from the field and 5-of-11 from three-point range, producing a dominant performance in just 32 minutes. “It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding. So I haven’t reached it as many times as I should have.” Wembanyama did not identify anyone as the target of that remark. However, the comment added another layer to a remarkable night that helped San Antonio improve to 14-3, matching the NBA’s best record. This was his second 50-point performance of the season and the third of his career. He previously scored a career-high 52 against the Dallas Mavericks on November 4. His latest effort tied David Robinson for the second-most 50-point games in Spurs history, behind George Gervin’s five. Wembanyama established control early, scoring 17 first-quarter points before reaching halftime with 32 points and 13 rebounds. The Spurs led 61-45 at the break, with their centerpiece influencing the game at both ends. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. “That step-back three that I took, it doesn’t correlate with this. It didn’t fit the definition, for example. So I did try, at the end, yeah, I did try to get a three when I had 47 points.” That admission gave his earlier remark an amusing contradiction. Wembanyama had teased others about chasing numbers, then openly conceded that he wanted the extra three points himself. He defended that instinct by referencing Wilt Chamberlain . “I don’t think Wilt thought about that when he had 98 points. I don’t think he thought about making the extra pass.” There is a reasonable distinction between enjoying a milestone and compromising a team’s chances to reach one. Wembanyama’s scoring came with exceptional efficiency, overwhelming rebounding, and substantial defensive production in a comfortable victory. His contribution extended far beyond the points column. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson also acknowledged that removing him just short of 50 would have been difficult, while emphasizing the importance of avoiding unnecessary injury risk. Ultimately, Wembanyama gave fans both a spectacular performance and a memorable sound bite. The stat-padding remark invited debate, but his willingness to admit chasing the final basket kept it from becoming a simple lecture directed at everyone else. At 22, he is already producing nights that require very little embellishment.

item.title: ESPN icon, Broncos legend Tom Jackson passes away at 75
item.description: The NFL and sports media worlds are in mourning, following the shocking news that Denver Broncos legend and ESPN icon Tom Jackson has passed away at age 75. The news was announced at the start of Sunday NFL Countdown ahead of Week 11. At the request of Jackson’s family, an emotional Chris Berman fought through tears to deliver the news while reading a statement. “All of us are stunned,” Berman said in a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned, and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet , Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown . “We’ve lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet.” Chris Berman announces the death of his longtime broadcast partner and best friend, Tom Jackson. What an iconic duo for all those years. Thank you, TJ ❤️ https://t.co/0eogqMa73r — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 22, 2026 “It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.” An official cause of death has not been announced at this time. Tom Jackson Was A Trail Blazer Sep 14, 2015; Atlanta, GA, USA; ESPN broadcaster Tom Jackson smiles prior to the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Atlanta Falcons at the Georgia Dome. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Before becoming a household name on ESPN, Jackson was a vaunted defender and member of the Broncos’ “Orange Crush” defense. As a player, Jackson was a fourth-round pick in 1973 out of Louisville, before becoming a two-time Pro Bowl during his 14 years with the Broncos. As an analyst, he was once again among the best, becoming a Hall of Fame broadcaster. Jackson retired from ESPN in 2016 after his final assignment, the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement ceremony alongside Berman. Berman said, “Tom long ago became almost a brother to me. I know every day he appeared on ESPN was a treasure for football fans.” Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and his two daughters, Taylor and Morgan. Our deepest condolences go out to Jackson’s family and friends during this incredibly difficult and tragic time. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Bayern Munich boss Herbert Hainer drops January transfer hint following Harry Kane and Michael Olise injury blows
item.description: FC Bayern München v 1. FC Köln - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their stance on the January transfer window after a devastating double injury blow to their attacking line. President Herbert Hainer admitted that while the club had not planned to spend, the sudden loss of key stars has forced the German giants to remain alert to market opportunities. Crisis at the Allianz Arena The tactical planning for Vincent Kompany has become a genuine nightmare following a string of fitness issues that have decimated his offensive options. The headline news is the loss of star striker Harry Kane , who is facing a recovery period of three to four months after suffering a syndesmosis tear in his left ankle during the recent 1-1 draw against Koln . This follows existing injuries to Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, and Alphonso Davies, leaving the Bundesliga leaders short of proven goalscoring pedigree. Adding to the frustration, Olise is also expected to miss the upcoming Champions League clash with Lille. While his foot injury was initially diagnosed as only a bruise, the recovery timeline remains tight. The lack of senior options is so severe that Kompany may have to rely on teenagers to lead the line. Transfer U-turn on the cards Before this weekend, the hierarchy in Munich had reportedly decided against making any mid-season moves, even with high-profile free agents like Jadon Sancho or Karim Benzema theoretically available. However, the severity of the current situation has forced a shift in tone from the boardroom. Club president Herbert Hainer admitted that the club is now keeping a "back door" open for potential winter reinforcements should the injury list fail to clear up as expected before the new year. Hainer was candid about the unexpected nature of the recent setbacks when speaking to the press. "The fact is that it is a situation that we did not expect - that must be clearly stated. I don't think we'll have to react again in the winter break, but you see how quickly it can go. Now we've had two more injuries since Friday. If it had to be, FC Bayern is always able to react. But it is not our wish," the president said, as quoted by BILD . Managing the remaining stars While Luis Diaz and Jamal Musiala are returning to fitness, the club is cautious about rushing them back into the starting lineup and risking further long-term absences. Director of sport Max Eberl highlighted the need for a delicate approach with the players currently available to Kompany. "With Jamal and with all the boys we have now, we have to be careful," the sporting director warned, noting that results must still be achieved despite the depleted squad depth. The immediate focus remains on the next seven fixtures before the Christmas break, where Bayern must navigate a difficult schedule with a makeshift attack. Adding to the frustration, Olise is also expected to miss the upcoming Champions League clash with Lille. While his foot injury was initially diagnosed as only a bruise, the recovery timeline remains tight. The lack of senior options is so severe that Kompany may have to rely on teenagers to lead the line. However, the severity of the current situation has forced a shift in tone from the boardroom. I don't think we'll have to react again in the winter break, but you see how quickly it can go. Now we've had two more injuries since Friday. If it had to be, FC Bayern is always able to react. But it is not our wish," the president said, as quoted by BILD . Managing the remaining stars While Luis Diaz and Jamal Musiala are returning to fitness, the club is cautious about rushing them back into the starting lineup and risking further long-term absences. Director of sport Max Eberl highlighted the need for a delicate approach with the players currently available to Kompany. "With Jamal and with all the boys we have now, we have to be careful," the sporting director warned, noting that results must still be achieved despite the depleted squad depth. The immediate focus remains on the next seven fixtures before the Christmas break, where Bayern must navigate a difficult schedule with a makeshift attack. Eberl was firm in his demand for professional standards despite the adversity. "We still have to perform. We don't need to talk big now. We have this squad as it is now. And with it, we simply have to try to get results in the next seven games," he stated during his post-match assessment. Youth talent steps into the spotlight Kompany has been forced to look deep into the club's academy, handing a debut to 19-year-old Noah Codjo-Evora in the closing stages of the Koln match. Other prospects like 16-year-old Bastian Assomo, who has been in sensational form for Germany's U17 side, are also being considered for inclusion. However, the Belgian coach is determined to maintain a sense of calm within the dressing room rather than succumbing to the pressure of the mounting injury crisis. The manager is staying focused on the collective effort rather than individual savior narratives. "I'm not a fan of panic in football. So: now calmly make a plan together and fight without end. But really! And then get our results. And who will then play a role, we can't say yet," Kompany remarked.

item.title: Did beaten Wales still show they have come a long way?
item.description: Wales won three Tests at Principality Stadium in 2026 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] For experienced hooker Ryan Elias, the proof of Wales' progress came when he looked around in the post-match huddle and saw heads down after a narrow defeat by Australia. Steve Tandy's side failed to back up their historic victory against New Zealand when edged out 28-25 by the Wallabies in the Nations Championship. Wales could not claim another scalp against the Aussies, who are two places above them in seventh in World Rugby's rankings, but went close. "It wasn't that long ago, not even 12 months ago, that we probably would have been chuffed with that result," said 54-times capped Scarlets forward Elias. "You look around the circle at the end of that game and there were boys with heads down because this is one that got away. "That just shows the growth of the group and the belief that's coming." Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat Wales should have picked Botham, says flanker's dad Next Sunday is the one-year anniversary of Wales' 73-0 defeat by South Africa in Cardiff, a hammering that was followed by heavy Six Nations losses against England and France. Tandy's squad have since enjoyed victories against Italy, Fiji and Japan before the statement success against New Zealand. "It's hard to recreate what they did against the All Blacks," former Wales centre Tom Shanklin said on Scrum V podcast. "It's hard to get to that level every week but it was really positive. We're still in a building phase. "We said the best thing about the Japan game was that it was a bonus-point win, and that was about it. "That feels a long time ago. We've come a long, long way. "The effort was there against Australia, but there just wasn't that clinical edge and maybe that's a psychological thing." Wales were nervy 28-21 winners at the start of November against a Japan side who have since been thumped by England and Scotland. They face the Brave Blossoms again on Saturday (13:10 GMT) at Nations Championship finals weekend at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. "This is a big game now to see how much we've changed and developed from the first game of the campaign to the last," said Shanklin. Sherratt sharpening up Wales' attack Wales chalked up four-try bonuses in all three games in Cardiff and have added to their threat from driving line-out. They have profited from consistency at 10-12-13 with Sam Costelow, Max Llewellyn and Eddie James. "You're seeing a team that seems to have found an attack," said Shanklin. "Matt Sherratt has worked really hard with them and we've got various options now, we're not too predictable. "We're playing with a lot more quick ball and we're quite clever in how we're breaking teams down. "There are multiple options now when taking the ball to the line and we are getting it into the hands of our strike runners." Wales did, however, waste a number of 22 entries in the first half and the final try by Ryan Elias came after pressure that ate into the clock. "

Wales could not claim another scalp against the Aussies, who are two places above them in seventh in World Rugby's rankings, but went close. "It wasn't that long ago, not even 12 months ago, that we probably would have been chuffed with that result," said 54-times capped Scarlets forward Elias. "You look around the circle at the end of that game and there were boys with heads down because this is one that got away. "That just shows the growth of the group and the belief that's coming." Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat Wales should have picked Botham, says flanker's dad Next Sunday is the one-year anniversary of Wales' 73-0 defeat by South Africa in Cardiff, a hammering that was followed by heavy Six Nations losses against England and France. Tandy's squad have since enjoyed victories against Italy, Fiji and Japan before the statement success against New Zealand. "It's hard to recreate what they did against the All Blacks," former Wales centre Tom Shanklin said on Scrum V podcast. "It's hard to get to that level every week but it was really positive. We're still in a building phase. "We said the best thing about the Japan game was that it was a bonus-point win, and that was about it. "That feels a long time ago. We've come a long, long way. "The effort was there against Australia, but there just wasn't that clinical edge and maybe that's a psychological thing." Wales were nervy 28-21 winners at the start of November against a Japan side who have since been thumped by England and Scotland. They face the Brave Blossoms again on Saturday (13:10 GMT) at Nations Championship finals weekend at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. "This is a big game now to see how much we've changed and developed from the first game of the campaign to the last," said Shanklin. Sherratt sharpening up Wales' attack Wales chalked up four-try bonuses in all three games in Cardiff and have added to their threat from driving line-out. They have profited from consistency at 10-12-13 with Sam Costelow, Max Llewellyn and Eddie James. "You're seeing a team that seems to have found an attack," said Shanklin. "Matt Sherratt has worked really hard with them and we've got various options now, we're not too predictable. "We're playing with a lot more quick ball and we're quite clever in how we're breaking teams down. "There are multiple options now when taking the ball to the line and we are getting it into the hands of our strike runners." Wales did, however, waste a number of 22 entries in the first half and the final try by Ryan Elias came after pressure that ate into the clock. "We were really good up to about five or 10 metres out, then we lost the detail," said former Wales and Lions wing Alex Cuthbert on Scrum V. "We didn't do a lot to get held up over the line. We were quite predictable around the corner and Australia won every physical battle and were very good defensively." Is Rees-Zammit even better than before? Louis Rees-Zammit vowed in the summer that he would fire in his second season back in rugby after his crack at the NFL. The 6ft 2ins wing has been true to his word and arguably the 2021 Lions tourist is a better player now than he was before heading to America in 2024. Rees-Zammit provided more evidence of his pace and added power when creating Blair Murray's try down the right in the second half. "I was in line with where Zam had the ball and thought that surely Harry Potter was not going to give him the outside," said Cuthbert. "It was only three or four yards and he did a shimmy in and if he gets half a yard outside then he is so quick. "But now he is so strong from the hip down, so broke through Potter and then [Joseph-Aukuso] Suaalii tried to come across and it looked like they got an arm on him. "It's just that power and watch Rees-Zammit carry now and he makes yard after contact." The Bristol back has returned to wing and Murray, one of Wales' star performers in 2024-25, has profited from starting at full-back. "He's a class player isn't he?" said the Scarlets man about Rees-Zammit. "He is one of the best wingers in the world, and he shows it week in and week out. "We're working well together, you know. Whether I'm putting him through holes or he's getting through and passing it back inside. "That connection is growing and we want to get the ball in our hands as much as we can." The pair and experienced wing Josh Adams look sure to start the Six Nations, fitness permitting. Tandy's big selection calls Alex Mann started every game in the 2026 Six Nations [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Tandy opted to change a winning team, going back to the starters that faced Japan. His decision to rest flanker James Botham is in the spotlight after his man-of-the-match display against the All Blacks. Alex Mann was to the fore in a different way despite suffering a painful early poke in the eye from team-mate Ben Carter, coming up with a turnover, claiming five line-outs and riling the Wallabies. "You're certainly looking at the squad now thinking you're a lot more confident if there are injuries," said Shanklin. "To have strength and depth with two quality players in every single position then you have got to play them. "You cannot just have your first team out every game, then when players come in they are not going to be up to that level or have that experience. You've got to mix and match a bit." Tandy is poised to rotate his squad for Saturday's fixture against Japan, when Wales travel to London after three games on home soil. It will be the first game of a double-header and a warm-up for England's rematch with New Zealand. Wales will play two home games in the 2027 Six Nations [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales win against the All Blacks gave a boost to ticket sales for the Wallabies fixture despite the late kick-off time. The crowd of 66,307 was larger than the 52,425 against Japan and 55,152 against New Zealand. Crucially, after the lows of last season's heavy defeats by South Africa and France, the connection seems strong between Tandy's team and the supporters. "The atmosphere was amazing again," said Cuthbert, who scored two tries in the bedlam of the famous 2013 victory against England. "You've got to give credit to the Principality Stadium staff, they are really making the place have that bit of theatre and entertainment." Wales will hope it gives them an extra lift for the visits of Ireland and England in the Six Nations. Nations Championship finals weekend - who plays who?

item.title: Eric DeCosta Is Officially On the Hot Seat
item.description: General Manager Eric DeCosta has failed to build a complete team around Lamar Jackson . The Baltimore Ravens have reached a point where their problems can no longer be blamed on one injury or one bad performance. Their recent 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers exposed a roster with too many weaknesses. Baltimore started off the season with a 4-1 record, but they’re now sitting at 4-6. Jackson’s absence has certainly hurt the offense. But a team that’s built to contend for a Super Bowl should not completely fall apart when its franchise quarterback can’t play. The Ravens have struggled to run the ball and protect their other four quarterbacks while also not being able to stop opposing offenses. These problems raise serious questions about DeCosta and the way he has constructed this roster. Baltimore has invested heavily in established players, but a majority of those investments have not produced the expected results. DeCosta has had multiple years to address certain weaknesses, yet the same problems continue to hurt the team. The Ravens Cannot Function Without Lamar Jackson The biggest concern with Baltimore’s roster is how dependent the team has become on Jackson. His absence has exposed how little the offense can accomplish without him. Before Jacoby Brissett ‘s start, Baltimore averaged 103.4 yards per quarter with Jackson on the field, compared to just 67.6 without him. Jackson has already dealt with multiple injuries this season. He suffered an ankle injury against Tennessee and a thumb injury against Buffalo that required surgery. Even with Jackson under contract through 2027, Baltimore cannot keep putting him in spots where he has to carry the roster year after year. The remaining players must be capable of producing when he is unavailable. DeCosta deserves criticism for failing to build enough depth around Jackson. A roster with championship expectations should have more answers when its starting quarterback goes down. Eric DeCosta Has Failed to Fix the Offensive Line The offensive line has been Baltimore’s biggest concern for multiple seasons. Despite repeated attempts to address the position, the unit continues to struggle. They kept putting Jackson in tough situations. In fact, Tyler Huntley is now out for the season after being sacked. In addition to being ineffective in pass protection, the team has also faced problems with the running game. Going into Week 9, the Ravens offensive line had seen 25 different combinations of players, which was the highest in the NFL at that point in time. Though some of the changes can be attributed to injuries, it shows how difficult it has been to assemble a reliable group. item.content:encoded: General Manager Eric DeCosta has failed to build a complete team around Lamar Jackson . The Baltimore Ravens have reached a point where their problems can no longer be blamed on one injury or one bad performance. Their recent 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers exposed a roster with too many weaknesses. Baltimore started off the season with a 4-1 record, but they’re now sitting at 4-6. Jackson’s absence has certainly hurt the offense. But a team that’s built to contend for a Super Bowl should not completely fall apart when its franchise quarterback can’t play. The Ravens have struggled to run the ball and protect their other four quarterbacks while also not being able to stop opposing offenses. These problems raise serious questions about DeCosta and the way he has constructed this roster. Baltimore has invested heavily in established players, but a majority of those investments have not produced the expected results. DeCosta has had multiple years to address certain weaknesses, yet the same problems continue to hurt the team. The Ravens Cannot Function Without Lamar Jackson The biggest concern with Baltimore’s roster is how dependent the team has become on Jackson. His absence has exposed how little the offense can accomplish without him. Before Jacoby Brissett ‘s start, Baltimore averaged 103.4 yards per quarter with Jackson on the field, compared to just 67.6 without him. Jackson has already dealt with multiple injuries this season. He suffered an ankle injury against Tennessee and a thumb injury against Buffalo that required surgery. Even with Jackson under contract through 2027, Baltimore cannot keep putting him in spots where he has to carry the roster year after year. The remaining players must be capable of producing when he is unavailable. DeCosta deserves criticism for failing to build enough depth around Jackson. A roster with championship expectations should have more answers when its starting quarterback goes down. Eric DeCosta Has Failed to Fix the Offensive Line The offensive line has been Baltimore’s biggest concern for multiple seasons. Despite repeated attempts to address the position, the unit continues to struggle. They kept putting Jackson in tough situations. In fact, Tyler Huntley is now out for the season after being sacked. In addition to being ineffective in pass protection, the team has also faced problems with the running game. Going into Week 9, the Ravens offensive line had seen 25 different combinations of players, which was the highest in the NFL at that point in time. Though some of the changes can be attributed to injuries, it shows how difficult it has been to assemble a reliable group. This offensive line group is ranked 26th by PFF after getting ranked 16th last season. In fact, there is even an entire compilation on the internet of Ravens quarterbacks repeatedly taking hits. The repeated pressure raises further concerns about Baltimore’s offensive-line protection. DeCosta has had multiple seasons to address this position, yet the Ravens continue to struggle with consistency. His inability to build a more reliable offensive line has left the team’s quarterbacks vulnerable to constant pressure. The o-line dilemma has directly impacted Derrick Henry , as he has only been averaging 3.8 yards per carry . In fact, last week against the Chargers, the Ravens ran for a mere 16 rushing yards. The Ravens ran for zero — 0 — yards in the 1st half, which are the fewest in a first half in franchise history. Derrick Henry was hit at or behind the line of scrimmage on 4 of his 5 carries in the first half. — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) November 17, 2026 Expensive Contracts and a Defense That Has Not Delivered The Ravens have invested heavily in their defense, but the results have fallen short of expectations. Baltimore has been struggling on defense the past two seasons. DeCosta spent around $187 million on the Ravens’ defense. With that much money being spent, it is catastrophic how poor Baltimore’s defense has been, as they rank outside the top 10 for every defensive category. Key and veteran players like Roquan Smith , Marlon Humphrey , Nnamdi Madubuike , and Trey Hendrickson give Baltimore talent across the defense. However, having established names on the roster does not automatically create a successful unit. The Chargers entered Monday’s game scoring 15.1 points per game . However, they still managed to score 23 points against the Ravens, rushing for 160 rushing yards . That performance raises questions about the value Baltimore is getting from its defensive investments. Smith, Humphrey, and most of the high-paid players have been seen as stars on paper, but they have not played to that expectation. The same contract question applies across the roster with other established veterans like Ronnie Stanley , Mark Andrews , and John Simpson . most expensive defenses in 2026 $193.0M – Steelers $187.4M – Ravens $177.7M – Bears $174.7M – Giants $169.0M – Patriots $165.8M – Commanders $159.6M – Seahawks $148.3M – Titans $147.3M – Colts $147.0M – Raiders $145.5M – Panthers $142.1M – Broncos $141.6M – Chiefs $140.2M -… — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) June 5, 2026 Why Eric DeCosta’s Job Is Now in Question DeCosta must be held accountable for how he has allocated the team’s financial resources. Baltimore has committed significant money to players who haven’t consistently justified their contracts. This limits the team’s ability to address a lot of weaknesses in this squad. Those decisions could create bigger salary-cap problems for the Ravens moving forward. Baltimore has yet to reach a Super Bowl with Jackson despite having Super Bowl expectations. Instead of maximizing that window, DeCosta has built shaky trenches on both sides of the ball. Overpaying aging veterans and making reactive trades only deepens the roster’s flaws. Falling to a winless Chargers team just exposed what happens when a general manager misses on the details. Simply put, DeCosta has not fixed these recurring mistakes, putting himself on the hot seat and wasting Jackson’s prime.
