item.content:encoded: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement. ﻿ Wike argued that though the removal of fuel subsidy came with initial difficulties, it would be in the best interest of Nigeria and its people for the President to complete the foundation he has laid for the country’s recovery and prosperity. He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition campaign council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections. Wike Wike, who said the campaigns would begin on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader who took difficult decisions to prevent Nigeria from collapsing. “This country was on the verge of collapse, on the verge of collapse, but by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” the former governor said. The minister cited the relative stability in the university system, saying lecturers’ strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic calendars, are no longer a recurring problem under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in securing their payments, arguing that the President’s decisions were necessary to address the country’s challenges. Wike described the removal of the fuel subsidy as one such difficult decision, acknowledging it came with disadvantages but insisting the challenges were temporary. “Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages. “And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity,” he said. “If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said. The minister called on Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers to support the re-election bid, insisting that the campaign would not discriminate on religious grounds. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters,” he added. “The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.” Wike also defended the Tinubu administration against claims of religious imbalance in its appointments, saying Christians benefited more from the government than under previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” said the minister. He further urged the congregation to participate actively in the forthcoming elections, warning that those who refuse to vote would have to live with the consequences of decisions made by others. “If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you,” he added. On the Rivers State governorship race, he urged the people to support the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Kingsley Chinda, describing him as a son of the soil. Speaking further, the minister said the dedication of the campaign council was in keeping with their tradition of committing political campaigns to God before setting out, expressing confidence that the exercise would be peaceful. “Just as we have never had a crisis before, I believe we will also not have a crisis in this period,” Wike said. The minister said he would continue to support the church. As part of his support for the church, Wike announced, on behalf of the Rainbow Coalition, his friends and associates, a donation of ₦100 million. He described the donation as their way of encouraging the church, urging religious leaders to also support them through prayers and the congregation through their votes. Members of the Rainbow Coalition, including Chinda, Chairman of the PDP Board of Trustees, Senator Mao Ohuabunwa, Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, Martin Amaewhule, and other political leaders, were present at the service. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s ally dismisses Fubara’s 3m votes pledge to Tinubu
item.description: …Insists Rivers is nobody’s political inheritance, says APC must be punished for emergency rule By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and close ally of its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, Chief Eze Chukwuemeka Eze, has dismissed Governor Siminalayi Fubara’s pledge to deliver three million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election. Eze described the governor’s assurance as an unrealistic political projection, insisting that Rivers State was not the political inheritance of any individual or group. Fubara had, on November 7, during a Rainbow Coalition/APC presidential rally in Port Harcourt, assured Tinubu that the people of Rivers would deliver at least three million votes for him in the January 2027 presidential election. Reacting to the pledge in a statement issued in Port Harcourt at the weekend, Eze described it as an “audacious exercise in political delusion, electoral deception and monumental grandstanding”. He argued that the projection was unattainable and disconnected from the prevailing political realities in the state, alleging that the governor made the promise to massage the President’s ego and create an impression of widespread political acceptance. The ADC chieftain said Tinubu’s reliance on political assurances from Fubara and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, showed a misunderstanding of the political consciousness of Rivers people and their grievances over the political crisis that engulfed the state. Eze recalled the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers, the suspension of the governor, his deputy and members of the State House of Assembly, insisting that the people had neither forgotten nor forgiven the circumstances surrounding the intervention. He said Rivers people were politically enlightened enough to distinguish genuine leadership from political manoeuvring and would not surrender their electoral choices to intimidation, patronage or political inducements. “It is rather amusing that President Tinubu appears to have mistaken political silence for political acquiescence and the orchestrated jubilation at Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium for an irrevocable endorsement of his administration,” he said. Eze also cautioned against interpreting the crowd at the APC rally as an indication of the President’s electoral strength in the state. “Let nobody deceive the President with the political theatrics of Nyesom Wike, Governor Siminalayi Fubara and their respective political establishments. “The crowd assembled at the stadium, regardless of its numerical appearance, cannot be substituted for the electorate. A rented or politically mobilised crowd, no matter how imposing, does not constitute an electoral mandate,” he said. He further predicted that Tinubu would struggle to secure 100,000 genuine votes in Rivers in 2027, adding that even such a figure would not necessarily amount to an endorsement of his administration. item.content:encoded: …Insists Rivers is nobody’s political inheritance, says APC must be punished for emergency rule By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and close ally of its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, Chief Eze Chukwuemeka Eze, has dismissed Governor Siminalayi Fubara’s pledge to deliver three million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election. Eze described the governor’s assurance as an unrealistic political projection, insisting that Rivers State was not the political inheritance of any individual or group. Fubara had, on November 7, during a Rainbow Coalition/APC presidential rally in Port Harcourt, assured Tinubu that the people of Rivers would deliver at least three million votes for him in the January 2027 presidential election. Reacting to the pledge in a statement issued in Port Harcourt at the weekend, Eze described it as an “audacious exercise in political delusion, electoral deception and monumental grandstanding”. He argued that the projection was unattainable and disconnected from the prevailing political realities in the state, alleging that the governor made the promise to massage the President’s ego and create an impression of widespread political acceptance. The ADC chieftain said Tinubu’s reliance on political assurances from Fubara and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, showed a misunderstanding of the political consciousness of Rivers people and their grievances over the political crisis that engulfed the state. Eze recalled the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers, the suspension of the governor, his deputy and members of the State House of Assembly, insisting that the people had neither forgotten nor forgiven the circumstances surrounding the intervention. He said Rivers people were politically enlightened enough to distinguish genuine leadership from political manoeuvring and would not surrender their electoral choices to intimidation, patronage or political inducements. “It is rather amusing that President Tinubu appears to have mistaken political silence for political acquiescence and the orchestrated jubilation at Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium for an irrevocable endorsement of his administration,” he said. Eze also cautioned against interpreting the crowd at the APC rally as an indication of the President’s electoral strength in the state. “Let nobody deceive the President with the political theatrics of Nyesom Wike, Governor Siminalayi Fubara and their respective political establishments. “The crowd assembled at the stadium, regardless of its numerical appearance, cannot be substituted for the electorate. A rented or politically mobilised crowd, no matter how imposing, does not constitute an electoral mandate,” he said. He further predicted that Tinubu would struggle to secure 100,000 genuine votes in Rivers in 2027, adding that even such a figure would not necessarily amount to an endorsement of his administration. The ADC chieftain also accused the President and his political associates of assuming that they could influence the judiciary, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to determine the outcome of the 2027 elections. He warned that such assumptions could undermine democracy, stressing that the institutions were established by the Constitution and should not serve the interests of any political party or administration. Eze said the Rivers political crisis had exposed the dangers of political arrogance, executive overreach and the subordination of constitutional democracy to personal political interests. He added that Nigerians facing economic hardship and what he described as failed governance would use the ballot box to express their dissatisfaction and determine the country’s political future. The ADC chieftain insisted that Rivers State was not the political property of any individual, warning that neither political alliances nor the influence of power brokers could guarantee electoral support. He said the 2027 elections would ultimately be determined by voters, not political promises, rallies or claims of control over the electorate. item.title: Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise
item.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity. Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X handle on Sunday while reacting to Tinubu’s message in Ibadan that Nigeria was on the path to prosperity. He argued that Nigerians needed to see improvements in their living conditions, particularly in the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential services. According to him, the President should explain the achievements of his administration and how its policies have translated into better living conditions for citizens, especially as he seeks another term in 2027. Ibe questioned how long households would have to contend with rising living expenses, while workers struggle with increasing costs and businesses face energy-related challenges. He maintained that government claims of economic progress should be assessed against the everyday experiences of Nigerians. On the reported agreement to reopen a vehicle assembly plant, Ibe said productive investment was welcome but argued that its benefits should be measured by the actual resumption of operations, employment opportunities and wider economic impact. He also acknowledged the importance of infrastructure development, while stressing that government should equally account for its impact on the livelihoods of citizens. Ibe further questioned the emphasis on future generations in the President’s appeal for Nigerians to remain committed to the administration’s policies, saying the immediate needs of children and struggling households should also receive attention. He called on the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a clear account of the outcomes of the sacrifices associated with its policies, including the benefits recorded and when households could expect meaningful relief. Reacting to Tinubu’s remarks about the opposition, Ibe said opposition parties had a legitimate role in scrutinising the administration’s performance, while citizens were entitled to consider alternative political positions. He argued that public confidence in government should be strengthened through responses to citizens’ concerns and demonstrable improvements in their living conditions. Ibe said the benefits of prosperity should be reflected in household purchasing power, workers’ wages, the survival of businesses and the security of communities. He maintained that the administration should provide evidence of its achievements and address the economic and security concerns confronting Nigerians. The post Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Emir of Daura trends on X after tourist’s ‘inappropriate touching’ allegation
item.description: The Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has become a subject of controversy on X after a female tourist accused him of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State. The allegation followed the circulation of a video on social media which appears to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit. The woman, who identifies herself online as ‘beduina’, made the allegation in an Instagram post after completing a 30-day trip across different parts of Nigeria. She said the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. Recounting the encounter, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room, where she sat with the traditional ruler and engaged in a conversation. She alleged that the Emir held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek. According to her, the encounter took a disturbing turn when the traditional ruler allegedly touched her breasts. “That was a shock for me. I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’, ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote. The tourist said she was particularly disturbed that the alleged incident happened inside a palace, despite having travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said. She described the experience as disgusting, adding that she had continued to relive the encounter in her thoughts. The woman said the incident happened a week before she made the allegation public but explained that she waited until she had left Nigeria before speaking about it. She also suggested that other women might have experienced similar treatment from the traditional ruler, although she did not provide evidence of such incidents. “I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. I have meta glasses and quickly turned them on,” she added. Her allegation has generated reactions on X, with some users expressing concern and demanding accountability. As of the time of filing this report, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation. The post Emir of Daura trends on X after tourist’s ‘inappropriate touching’ allegation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 70-year-old woman rescued after falling into 60ft well in Lagos
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni A 70-year-old woman has survived after accidentally falling into a 60-foot-deep well at Oworonshoki, Kosofe Local Government Area of Lagos State. The incident occurred in the early hours of Sunday at 37, Abiola Street, prompting a distress call to the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service. Firefighters from the Oworonshoki Fire Station promptly responded to the call and successfully rescued the septuagenarian alive. The rescue operation was concluded after the victim was stabilised and handed over to her family. The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, who confirmed the incident, said the woman was responding to treatment as of press time. The post 70-year-old woman rescued after falling into 60ft well in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rema & Wizkid Have Us Singing Along to “Feel Alright” With This New Lyric Video
item.description: Scene from the official lyric video for Rema and Wizkid’s “Feel Alright” off the seven-track EP E-Mortal Boy (EMB). If you have been singing along to “ Feel Alright ” since E-Mortal Boy came out, Rema has just dropped the official lyric video so you can finally catch every single line without guessing. Having the words on screen makes it much easier to follow how Rema and Wizkid trade verses on the opening track, mixing smooth R&B-leaning melodies with English, Nigerian Pidgin and Yoruba slang as they serenade a love interest. For plenty of listeners, “Feel Alright” is the biggest talking point on E-Mortal Boy because it marks the very first official collaboration between Rema and Wizkid, bringing two distinct Afrobeats eras together right at the start of the project. Putting out a lyric video for the track gives fans of both artists a chance to properly take in the lyrics and harmonies that have had the song on heavy rotation since the project landed. The release also keeps the spotlight on E-Mortal Boy, Rema’s seven-track EP that followed earlier singles “TEA” and “Oh No”. Alongside “Feel Alright” with Wizkid, the project includes “Velvet”, “TANZANIA” with BNYX, “SUGA” with Theodora , and closer “Bang Bang” with London and Kah-Lo , showing off the wide range of sounds Rema pulls together across the seven songs. If you have been waiting to learn every word of Rema and Wizkid’s first joint record, this lyric video has you covered. Watch below The post Rema & Wizkid Have Us Singing Along to “Feel Alright” With This New Lyric Video appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Atiku’s aide faults Defence Ministry over Tinubu rally publicity
item.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has questioned the use of the Ministry of Defence’s official social media platforms to publicise a campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid. Ibe, in a post on his X handle on Sunday, faulted the ministry for allegedly using its official Facebook page and X account to announce the rally and publicise Defence Minister, General Christopher Musa’s inspection of the venue ahead of the event. He argued that the development raised concerns about the use of government communication platforms for partisan political activities. According to him, while providing security for a presidential visit falls within the legitimate responsibilities of the ministry, using its official platforms to promote a re-election campaign compromises the institutional neutrality expected of public institutions. Ibe noted that the Ministry of Defence was funded by taxpayers across different political affiliations and should, therefore, serve the interests of all Nigerians rather than those of a particular political party. He said Nigerians facing insecurity deserved information about government efforts to protect their communities and support military personnel, rather than publicity for political campaigns. He also questioned the confidence opposition parties and voters could have in the impartiality of state institutions if official government communication platforms were used to promote activities associated with the ruling party. Ibe called on the Defence Minister to explain the publication, ensure the removal of what he described as partisan campaign publicity and maintain a clear distinction between official government responsibilities and party activities. The post Atiku’s aide faults Defence Ministry over Tinubu rally publicity appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NAFDAC destroys N22.73bn fake, unsafe products, records 52 arrests
item.description: … 821 seizures, 179 premises shut in eight months By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed unwholesome products valued at approximately N22.73 billion, seized 821 products and secured 52 arrests in eight months as it intensified enforcement against unsafe and substandard regulated products. The agency disclosed that it carried out 5,542 enforcement activities, including 213 raids, between January and August 2026, while 179 premises were shut and 221 sanctions imposed. The figures formed part of major regulatory milestones presented by NAFDAC at the International Pharmaceutical Regulators Programme (IPRP) Management Committee Meeting in Prague, Czech Republic, held from November 18 to 19, 2026. The agency also reported progress in local pharmaceutical manufacturing, disclosing that more than 70 per cent of finished pharmaceutical products covered by its 5+5 policy and Ceiling 36 are now being manufactured in Nigeria. The development is expected to reduce dependence on imported medicines and strengthen the country’s medicine security. In its regulatory update, NAFDAC said it had sustained its World Health Organisation (WHO) Maturity Level 3 status and was working towards attaining Maturity Level 4, the highest level of the WHO Global Benchmarking Tool. It identified digital innovation as a critical component of the transition, citing the Integrated Regulatory Information Management System (IRIMS), Performance Management System (i-PMS), GMP Inspection (GMPi), Application and AI-assisted Technical Screening Tools (TST), and the revised Med Safety App. The revised application is designed to strengthen the reporting of adverse drug reactions and substandard and falsified medical products. NAFDAC also highlighted Nigeria’s growing influence in African pharmaceutical regulation, noting that it had emerged as a reference National Regulatory Authority, hosting regulatory authorities from Uganda, The Gambia, Mozambique and Côte d’Ivoire for technical capacity building and institutional benchmarking. Another milestone was Nigeria’s ratification of the African Medicines Agency (AMA) Treaty, with the instruments of ratification deposited on October 25, 2026. The agency said the achievements reflected the strategic leadership of its Director-General, Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, and ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional capacity, promote science-based regulation and deepen international regulatory cooperation. NAFDAC reaffirmed its commitment to protecting public health, strengthening Nigeria’s pharmaceutical industry and positioning the country as a leading regulatory authority in Africa. The post NAFDAC destroys N22.73bn fake, unsafe products, records 52 arrests appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, overhaul of water transport safety
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has called for an investigation into Friday’s fatal boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, urging the Federal and State Governments to strengthen safety measures on the nation’s waterways to prevent further loss of lives. Atiku said the tragedy, which claimed several lives, highlighted the risks faced by millions of Nigerians who rely on boats for daily transportation, particularly in riverine communities, and called for urgent government action to protect them. In a statement on Sunday, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, described the incident as a heartbreaking tragedy that had plunged the affected communities into mourning. He said the victims were travelling to honour a departed loved one when the accident occurred. “What makes this tragedy even more painful is that these were ordinary Nigerians who set out in love and solidarity to honour a departed loved one, only to meet their own untimely deaths on the waters,” Ologbondiyan said. “Bayelsa has lost fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners. No words can adequately capture the depth of grief now hanging over the affected communities.” Ologbondiyan commended local divers, the Marine Police, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other emergency responders for their efforts in the search and rescue operations. He, however, called for a thorough investigation into the cause of the mishap and stricter enforcement of regulations against boat overloading, the use of unseaworthy vessels and other unsafe practices. He said preventing similar accidents would require sustained government investment in safer water transportation. “The Federal and State Governments must prioritise the provision of standard and well-maintained boats, adequate life jackets, functional jetties and properly trained boat operators across riverine communities,” he stressed. “For millions of Nigerians in the Niger Delta and other riverine areas, water transportation is not a luxury; it is a daily necessity. Their safety must never be treated as an afterthought.” He also urged the Federal Government, Bayelsa State Government and relevant humanitarian agencies to provide immediate assistance to survivors and bereaved families. Such assistance, he said, should include medical care, psychosocial support and financial help with the burial of victims. Atiku commiserated with the bereaved families, the people of Ayama and Ukubie communities and the Bayelsa State Government, while praying for the repose of the deceased and the speedy recovery of those injured. The post Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, overhaul of water transport safety appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How Tamagotchis got us hooked on digital pets
item.description: If you were are a kid in the late 1990s, there's a near-100 percent chance you either had a Tamagotchi or knew someone who did. The tiny digital pets came out of nowhere and became an overnight sensation, as millions of kids signed up to parent a crying, hungry, constantly dirty creature. Until they went to school, anyway, at which point their parents were given some new responsibilities they neither asked for nor wanted. On this episode of Version History, we dig deep into the story of the Tamagotchi. That story has its 30th anniversary this week, even though the real craze only lasted a few years. David Pierce is joined by The Verge's Mia … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: PSG confirm Desire Doue ruled out for months with torn ACL
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue has suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, the reigning French and European champions confirmed on Sunday. Doue, 21, went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half of Saturday’s 3-2 Ligue 1 win at Nice and was stretchered off in tears. The French international will undergo surgery before the end of the month, PSG added in a brief statement, without specifying the expected length of his absence, which is likely to be a matter of months. Doue looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow him to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG have also lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. “It is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique said on Saturday night. The French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns. He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently. Vanguard News The post PSG confirm Desire Doue ruled out for months with torn ACL appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Church not a political party — Bishop Mike Okonkwo
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The Fountain of Life Church today held its Sunday service despite reports of a court injunction against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya. Addressing the crowded congregation, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya said he had not received any court injunction as reported, and stressed his unwavering love for the church. Members were said to have chanted “We love you” during the service. The story of the believer never ends in shame… Weeping may endure for a night… rejoice not over me, my enemies, when I fall…” Bishop Okonkwo urged members to remain calm and trust God. “Do you know the challenge of believers? When trials, temptations and difficulties come, we fall apart. item.title: ABUAD warns students against cultism, cybercrime
item.description: Varsity matriculates 2,442 students for 2026/2027 session By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), has warned newly admitted students against cultism, cybercrime, substance abuse and other social vices capable of undermining their education and future. The university also cautioned the students against examination malpractice, bullying and the irresponsible use of artificial intelligence, urging them to uphold discipline, integrity and academic excellence. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Smaranda Olarinde, gave the warning at the institution’s 18th matriculation ceremony held over the weekend, where 2,442 students were formally admitted for the 2026/2027 academic session. The figure comprises 2,089 regular undergraduate students, 77 Open and Distance Learning students and 276 part-time students. Giving a breakdown of the undergraduate admissions, Olarinde said 306 students were admitted into the College of Social and Management Sciences, 307 into Sciences, 275 into Pharmacy, 684 into Medicine and Health Sciences, 171 into Law and 346 into Engineering. Addressing the students, the vice-chancellor described their admission as an opportunity that required discipline, responsibility and commitment to academic excellence. She urged them to be mindful of their associations, noting that their choice of friends could influence their habits, reputation, academic performance and future. According to her, university education goes beyond obtaining certificates to include character formation, emotional maturity, leadership development and the acquisition of values needed to contribute meaningfully to society. Olarinde urged the students to uphold the university’s philosophy of Labour, Service and Integrity, stressing that hard work, selfless service and honesty should guide their academic and professional pursuits. She also cautioned against the misuse of artificial intelligence and other emerging digital technologies, warning students not to present machine-generated materials or another person’s intellectual work as their original research. “The company you keep will influence your habits, attitude, reputation and ultimately your destiny. Surround yourselves with people who encourage learning, discipline, honesty and constructive ambition. “Stay away from cultism, substance abuse, bullying, examination malpractice, cybercrime and every other form of misconduct that can destroy your future and bring disrepute to your family and this university. “No momentary pleasure or misguided friendship is worth the sacrifice of your education, character or good name,” she said. On the use of artificial intelligence, the vice-chancellor said the technology could support research, improve productivity and create new opportunities for learning, but should not replace independent thinking, genuine scholarship or personal integrity. “Use digital tools responsibly. item.title: The Wedding Countdown Is On! Diana Eneje & Pascal Godwin Celebrate Their Introduction in Royal Blue
item.description: Pascal Godwin in Rogue and Diana Eneje in Dova Bridals at their introduction ceremony, styled by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon. Diana Eneje and Pascal Godwin ‘s forever journey has begun, but first of all, introductions! Three months after Pascal proposed against the backdrop of Cape Town’s mountains and vineyards in August 2026, the Nigerian fashion influencer and entrepreneur and her Lagos-based businessman fiancé have taken another lovely step towards walking down the aisle. While they are not married just yet, the couple have officially held their introduction ceremony, bringing both families together ahead of their traditional and white weddings. For anyone unfamiliar with the tradition, the introduction is an important first step in many Nigerian weddings. It is when the couple’s families meet formally, exchange greetings, offer prayers and give their blessings as the relationship moves towards marriage. And while the main wedding celebrations are still ahead, Diana and Pascal have given us a first look at what we can expect from their wedding style. Diana Eneje and Pascal Godwin in coordinated royal blue looks by Dova Bridals and Rogue for their introduction ceremony. If you’ve followed Diana from her early modelling days and her appearance in Rema ‘s 2019 “ Dumebi ” music video to building her beauty brand, The Shine Cartel, you’ll know that fashion is always part of her story. Styled together by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon , the two stepped out in coordinated royal blue looks, with Dova Bridals creating Diana’s introduction dress that brought together lace, colourful woven fabric and satin. Diana Eneje wearing a custom royal blue beaded lace, woven fabric, and satin mermaid gown by Dova Bridals. Her dress featured an off-the-shoulder beaded lace bodice with a sweetheart neckline and short tiered sleeves. From the waist, it flowed into a chevron-patterned woven skirt featuring shades of red, green, gold and blue, before opening into a pleated royal blue satin mermaid hem. She completed the look with a matching beaded fan handbag, silver jewellery with dark stone accents and crystal-strapped blue heels, alongside a sleek updo with sculpted waves. Diana Eneje in her custom Dova Bridals royal blue beaded lace and woven introduction dress, styled by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon and photographed by Chuchu Ojekwe Pascal coordinated with Diana in a custom royal blue velvet traditional robe and trouser set by Rogue . Gold and silver geometric and botanical beadwork ran across the chest, shoulders and sleeves, continuing down to the fringed hem . He finished with a matching beaded cap, layered deep blue beads and a gold pendant, dark-tinted sunglasses, a gold wristwatch and dark velvet loafers, with a tall carved black walking staff completing his traditional look . item.title: NELFUND considers increase in N20,000 monthly student upkeep
item.description: By Joseph Erunke Millions of Nigerian students benefiting from the Federal Government’s student loan scheme may soon receive higher monthly upkeep allowances as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, considers a review of the current N20,000 payment amid mounting pressure from rising living costs. The possibility of an increase emerged as NELFUND acknowledged that the existing allowance might require adjustment to better reflect the financial realities facing students struggling to meet the costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities while pursuing their education. The fund’s Managing Director, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines,a TVC news programme, where he said the monthly upkeep payment was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new figure or a timeline for implementation, Sawyer signalled that an adjustment was being considered, raising expectations among students who have repeatedly complained that the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance is inadequate to survive on in the face of escalating prices. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The indication of a possible increase comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the purchasing power of students, many of whom depend on the NELFUND intervention to cushion the financial burden of higher education. With food prices, transportation fares, accommodation costs and other essential expenses continuing to weigh heavily on households, the N20,000 monthly upkeep has increasingly come under scrutiny over its capacity to provide meaningful relief to beneficiaries. However, Sawyer said any decision to increase the allowance would have to be carefully weighed against the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for the growing number of students enrolled in the scheme. He explained that while NELFUND was conscious of the need to improve students’ welfare, it could not make adjustments without considering the implications for the entire beneficiary population. “What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” Sawyer said. Beyond the proposed review by NELFUND, Sawyer disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was also considering an intervention aimed at providing students with more meaningful financial support to enable them to remain in school and successfully complete their academic programmes. Although he did not disclose the nature, scope or financial details of the proposed presidential intervention, the NELFUND chief suggested that the government was exploring ways to improve the level of assistance available to students. “I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” he said. The fund’s Managing Director, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines,a TVC news programme, where he said the monthly upkeep payment was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new figure or a timeline for implementation, Sawyer signalled that an adjustment was being considered, raising expectations among students who have repeatedly complained that the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance is inadequate to survive on in the face of escalating prices. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The indication of a possible increase comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the purchasing power of students, many of whom depend on the NELFUND intervention to cushion the financial burden of higher education. With food prices, transportation fares, accommodation costs and other essential expenses continuing to weigh heavily on households, the N20,000 monthly upkeep has increasingly come under scrutiny over its capacity to provide meaningful relief to beneficiaries. However, Sawyer said any decision to increase the allowance would have to be carefully weighed against the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for the growing number of students enrolled in the scheme. He explained that while NELFUND was conscious of the need to improve students’ welfare, it could not make adjustments without considering the implications for the entire beneficiary population. “What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” Sawyer said. Beyond the proposed review by NELFUND, Sawyer disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was also considering an intervention aimed at providing students with more meaningful financial support to enable them to remain in school and successfully complete their academic programmes. Although he did not disclose the nature, scope or financial details of the proposed presidential intervention, the NELFUND chief suggested that the government was exploring ways to improve the level of assistance available to students. “I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” he said. Sawyer further hinted that changes could be expected in the future, although he stopped short of making a definite commitment on when the review would be concluded or how much beneficiaries could receive if the allowance is increased. “I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added. The proposed review is coming at a time when the Federal Government’s student loan programme is expanding rapidly, with millions of applications received from students seeking financial assistance to pursue tertiary education. NELFUND’s figures indicate that the fund has disbursed ₦180.5 billion to students as upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024, while another N194.7 billion has been paid to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees. The combined disbursement of approximately N375.2 billion underscores the growing scale of the intervention, which is designed to reduce financial barriers to tertiary education and prevent students from abandoning their studies because of economic hardship. The fund has also recorded more than 2.5 million applications and about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions, reflecting the increasing demand for financial assistance under the scheme. Despite the growing reach of the programme, the adequacy of the monthly upkeep allowance remains a major concern, particularly for students who rely on it to meet their day-to-day needs without additional financial support from their families. While Sawyer’s remarks offer hope of a possible adjustment, students will have to wait for the Federal Government and NELFUND to announce the details of any new arrangement, including the proposed amount, eligibility considerations and commencement date. For now, the N20,000 monthly allowance remains in place, but the fund’s acknowledgment of a possible review, coupled with the President’s reported interest in a fresh intervention, suggests that the government may be considering a more substantial financial lifeline for students struggling to stay afloat. item.title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
item.description: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land. The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access. With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses. Read full article Comments

item.title: 30 Years Later, Sean Connery's Secret James Bond Thriller Is Officially Free on Streaming
item.description: Back in the 1990s, Michael Bay was really cooking. Before the slog that was 2001’s Pearl Harbor and his divisive Transformers movies that simultaneously hurt and enhanced his career by sidelining him for decades, Bay debuted as a director with a trio of really exciting movies that prioritized a fun experience for the viewer. First there was 1995’s Bad Boys , the Will Smith and Martin Lawrence buddy-cop film that became a popular franchise. He closed out the decade with the genre-defining end-of-the-world disaster film Armageddon . And in between those two, he gave us a tightly crafted thriller that is currently free to stream (with ads) on Pluto TV.

item.title: COP31 makes history as longest-ever UN climate conference
item.description: COP31 broke the record Sunday for the longest-ever UN climate conference, running 44 hours past its scheduled closing time as countries struggled to clinch a deal. The previous mark was held by COP25 in Madrid in 2019, which ended at 1:55 pm on Sunday instead of 6:00 pm on Friday, according to Earth Negotiations Bulletin, an independent reporting service that tracks UN treaty negotiations. item.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
item.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. The post Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ogun PDP deputy guber candidate installed Akinkanju of Egbaland
item.description: By Jimoh Babatunde The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Deputy Governorship Candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has been installed as the first Akinkanju of Egbaland by the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, Okukenu IV. The installation took place at the Alake Palace on Saturday as part of activities marking the monarch’s 21st coronation anniversary. Sowunmi-Kolapo, who was previously honoured with the title of Iyalode of Ijemo, is also the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State. According to the palace, the new title, the first of its kind, was conferred on her in recognition of her contributions to the development of Egbaland and her commitment to the community. Oba Gbadebo urged her to remain committed to service, cultural preservation and the promotion of unity across Egbaland. The ceremony attracted prominent personalities, including government officials, business leaders, traditional rulers and politicians. The Ogun State PDP governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, led other party leaders to celebrate with his running mate. Speaking at the reception held at the Abeokuta Sports Club, Sowunmi-Kolapo expressed gratitude for the honour, particularly acknowledging the Alake for the recognition. She also described the conferment as significant ahead of the 2027 governorship election, saying the people of Ogun State had spoken through the honour. The deputy governorship candidate maintained that the forthcoming election should transcend party affiliations, insisting that the people must resist any alleged attempt to undermine the state’s interests. “We are indigenes of Ogun State. We do not run from battles. It is in our DNA to always resist intimidation and protect our independence. “I’m humbled by this gracious conferment of the title of the 1st Akinkanju of Egbaland on me by His Royal Majesty. “I pray to justify the confidence reposed in me by our traditional rulers, our respected elders, who have continued to stand for our heritage, the people of Egbaland, and the people of Ogun State in general. “Our father, the Alake of Egbaland, has spoken. Let us work hard to continue to have an Egba community that is first among others,” she said. Also honoured at the ceremony was Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, who was installed as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland by the Alake. In his remarks, Adebutu congratulated his running mate and the other honourees, describing their recognition as well deserved. He said Sowunmi-Kolapo’s elevation from Iyalode of Ijemo to Akinkanju of Egbaland reflected her years of service, loyalty, courage, motherly leadership and commitment to the unity and development of the Egba people. Adebutu also congratulated Obasanjo on her installation as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland, describing the honour as recognition of her distinguished public service and contributions to Egbaland and Nigeria. He said the two traditional honours conferred by the Alake during

item.title: NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking
item.description: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment. The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance. According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall. A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes. Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport. The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted. During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically. He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags. The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments. It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist. She was subsequently arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on October 15 while attempting to board a South African Airways flight to Kenya. item.content:encoded: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment. The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance. According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall. A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes. Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport. The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted. During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically. He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags. The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments. It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist. She was subsequently arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on October 15 while attempting to board a South African Airways flight to Kenya. The 25-year-old private chef reportedly told investigators that she was recruited through a man who was introduced to her by a friend in Kenya and promised $8,000 upon successful delivery of the consignment. She said she travelled from Kenya to South Africa on October 4, stayed in a hotel for about a week and met Henlo at the airport on October 11, where he handed her two of the four boxes before they checked them in under their respective luggage tags. On arrival in Lagos, she allegedly collected the two boxes bearing the golfer’s tags before a driver took her to a hotel in the Lekki area. The claim tag for the two boxes bearing her name, which she reportedly abandoned at the airport, was recovered from her hand luggage. Both suspects subsequently identified each other during an identification parade. Other seizures, arrests In a separate operation at the import shed of the Lagos airport on November 13, NDLEA operatives intercepted a consolidated consignment that arrived from the United Kingdom aboard an Allied Air flight. The agency said a freight agent, Sobowale Oladayo, was arrested when he presented himself to clear the shipment. A search of the consignment led to the recovery of 10 parcels of synthetic cannabinoid weighing 10.10 kilogrammes, 27 packs of marshmallow weighing 318.80 kilogrammes and precursor chemicals comprising 11 containers of N,N-Dimethylformamide (DMF) weighing 18.90 kilogrammes, 10 containers of 5-Bromo-1-Pentane weighing 8.05 kilogrammes and seven containers of Potassium Carbonate weighing 7.60 kilogrammes. The total gross weight of the recovered items was 363.45 kilogrammes. In a follow-up operation on November 14, the agency arrested the consignee, identified as Kareem Issa, 35, also known as Ola, when he arrived to collect the shipment at a logistics company’s premises in a grey Lexus 460 SUV, accompanied by two other persons. The NDLEA said Issa, a plumber by profession who lives on Lagos Island, allegedly presented himself as a senior security personnel. Investigations reportedly showed that he routinely activated the siren fitted to his vehicle whenever he visited the logistics company to collect consignments, allegedly to portray himself as a security operative and avoid attention. In Kaduna State, operatives on patrol along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway at Jere on November 17 arrested a 35-year-old man, Lawali Muhammad, with 160 pieces of explosives allegedly being transported to Zamfara State. The intended recipient, identified as Aliyu Mohammed, 30, was subsequently arrested in a follow-up operation in Gusau on the same day. Also arrested along the Jere axis were two suspects, Yusuf Magaji and Buhari Yusuf, 32, with 6,900 tablets of tramadol 225mg, 20,000 tablets of diazepam and 25,000 tablets of Exol-5. Similarly, operatives along the Zaria-Kano Expressway at Gwargwaje, Zaria, recovered 627,500 capsules of tramadol weighing 21.50 kilogrammes from a Hummer bus whose driver reportedly abandoned the vehicle and fled upon sighting the officers. In Ogun State, a woman, Esther Ogundipe, was arrested on November 19 during a raid on a drug joint at Eleweran, Abeokuta, with two locally made firearms and five live cartridges. Two days earlier, two other female suspects, Balikis Ogunbiyi and Omobola Ajani, were arrested during a raid in Ilaro with 7.4 grammes of cocaine, 638 grammes of cannabis and 5.9 grammes of methamphetamine. In Osun State, a 43-year-old man, Francis Oduke, was arrested along the Ikire-Ibadan Expressway with 359 bags of skunk weighing 4,627.7 kilogrammes, concealed beneath a load of granite in a truck. In neighbouring Ondo State, operatives intercepted a truck conveying 93 bags of cannabis weighing 1,045 kilogrammes to Kano State along the Zango-Ado Expressway, Akure, on November 16. The agency said the interception followed intelligence gathering and surveillance of the vehicle, which was loaded in Ogbese town. Four suspects, Adamu Yerima, 19; Mohammed Mohammed, 19; Nura Mohammed, 25; and Usman Mohammed, were arrested in connection with the seizure. In Edo State, a 48-year-old man, Emmanuel Eze, was arrested on November 20 with 11 and a half bags of cannabis weighing 156 kilogrammes at Aduwawa community, Benin City. In Katsina State, operatives arrested a 39-year-old man, Abbas Bello, in the Gafai area on November 17 with 148 blocks of cannabis weighing 72 kilogrammes concealed in the boot of his white Honda Accord car. In Abia State, operatives on November 18 raided a shop belonging to a 25-year-old woman, Oluebube Innocent, at Amankwa Street, Obingwa Local Government Area, recovering two kilogrammes of cannabis concealed in a hole dug into the shop’s floor and covered with ceramic tiles. The tiles were removed to recover the substance. In Rivers State, a 46-year-old physically challenged man, Peter Sunday, was arrested with 300 grammes of cannabis during a raid in Eneka on November 17. item.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
item.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. Under the standard programme, eligible Economy Class passengers can receive one night in a four-star hotel, while Business Class passengers may receive two nights in a five-star or boutique hotel. item.content:encoded: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. Turkish Airlines: Turn Istanbul Into Part of Your Holiday Turkish Airlines operates a Stopover in Istanbul programme for eligible international passengers connecting through Istanbul Airport. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. Qualifying travellers with connections of at least 20 hours and up to seven days may receive complimentary hotel accommodation. Under the standard programme, eligible Economy Class passengers can receive one night in a four-star hotel, while Business Class passengers may receive two nights in a five-star or boutique hotel. Imagine travelling from Abuja or Lagos through Istanbul to London, Paris or another European destination. Rather than treating Istanbul as somewhere you simply change planes, you could plan time to experience the Grand Bazaar, the Bosphorus and the city’s extraordinary cultural heritage. The programme has specific conditions, including qualifying return tickets, participating countries of departure and an application made at least 72 hours before the relevant flight. The complimentary accommodation does not cover every expense. Airport transfers, visa fees and other personal costs remain your responsibility. And for Nigerian passport holders, permission to enter Türkiye must be established before departure. A hotel voucher is not a substitute for a visa. There is also Touristanbul, a separate complimentary sightseeing programme for eligible passengers with shorter connections, typically between six and 24 hours. The two programmes have different conditions and cannot simply be combined. Qatar Airways: A Stopover That Requires More Planning Qatar Airways offers an opportunity to turn a connection through Doha into an additional holiday. However, for Nigerian passport holders, there is an important distinction between the airline’s advertised stopover offers and the actual requirements for entering Qatar. While Qatar Airways promotes discounted stopover accommodation, Nigerian travellers should not assume they can access these packages without first satisfying Qatar’s visa requirements. Under the arrangement applicable to Nigerian travellers, obtaining the relevant visa requires purchasing an eligible Discover Qatar package with a minimum of three nights’ accommodation from accredited travel companies in Nigeria. This means the stopover is not necessarily an opportunity to enjoy complimentary or heavily discounted accommodation. Instead, its value lies in the possibility of incorporating Doha into an international journey without purchasing an entirely separate return flight from Nigeria. For example, if you are travelling from Lagos to Singapore through Doha, you could investigate a ticket that allows you to spend three nights in Qatar before continuing to Singapore. You would still need to budget for the qualifying Discover Qatar accommodation package, visa requirements, meals, activities and other expenses. The potential saving is therefore in the flight arrangement rather than the hotel. This is an important lesson about stopover programmes: what an airline advertises globally may not be equally accessible to every passport holder . Before booking, confirm your visa eligibility, the required Discover Qatar package and whether the extended stopover changes your airfare. Ethiopian Airlines: Discover Addis Ababa on Your Way to Another Destination For travellers heading to destinations across Africa and beyond, Ethiopian Airlines offers an opportunity worth investigating. Eligible passengers connecting through Addis Ababa for between eight and 24 hours on qualifying Ethiopian Airlines tickets can receive complimentary hotel accommodation, meals and airport transfers. The airline also offers sightseeing experiences through Ethiopian Holidays. Imagine flying from Abuja to Cape Town through Addis Ababa. Instead of spending a long connection inside the airport, you could use an eligible stopover to experience Ethiopian coffee culture, local cuisine and some of the capital’s attractions before continuing to South Africa. The airline generally issues accommodation vouchers to qualifying passengers at their departure airport or transit desk (but make sure you already have your visa before going to the desk). Passengers wishing to leave the airport must still satisfy Ethiopia’s entry requirements. The airline may assist with transit documentation under its qualifying programme, but this should be confirmed before travel. For me, this is an excellent example of how a journey through Africa can become an opportunity to discover more of the continent. Emirates: Understand the Difference Between Dubai Connect and a Dubai Holiday Dubai is already a familiar destination to many Nigerian travellers, but there is an important distinction between deliberately stopping in Dubai and qualifying for Emirates’ Dubai Connect service. Dubai Connect can provide accommodation and other transit assistance to eligible passengers with qualifying connections, generally between six and 26 hours. However, it is designed around the best available flight connection, not simply a passenger’s desire to extend a holiday. If you deliberately choose a much longer connection when a shorter eligible one exists, you may not qualify for the complimentary service. That does not mean you cannot plan Dubai into a wider holiday. You can investigate a paid multi-city itinerary or a ticket that allows a longer stay. UAE government is also constantly changing its rules, so make sure to check all this properly before booking that trip. For example, you might arrange Lagos to Dubai, spend several nights there, then continue to Bangkok or Singapore before returning home. But that is a planned multi-city journey, not necessarily a free airline s
